raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

#43304 asks for per-stage metrics on the multi-tokenizer / multi-detokenizer
IPC path so a saturated stage can be identified from metrics instead of
out-of-tree tracing. Its proposed metric 4 calls for per-message processing
time histograms in `MultiDetokenizerRouter` and in each detokenizer worker.
The router half is covered by #45036; the detokenizer worker half is not
covered by any open or merged PR (#43323 router CPU, #44390 router
throughput, #44524 per-process CPU labels, #46596 scheduler-to-router
delivery latency cover the other proposals).

This PR adds the detokenizer-side processing-time histogram, mirroring the
semantics of the router histogram in #45036 so the two stages can be
compared directly: which stage's processing time grows is where the work
piles up.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/managers/detokenizer_manager.py`: when
  `--enable-metrics` is on, `DetokenizerManager` now creates a
  `sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds` histogram next to the existing
  CPU monitor start, using the same bucket set as the router histogram in
  #45036, and wraps dispatch plus send in the timing context defined on
  the mixin. The receive wait stays outside the timed section, so
  queueing delay in the ZMQ socket is excluded.
- `python/sglang/srt/managers/multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: defines the `_timed_processing` context manager on the
  mixin (a no-op that never reads the clock when no histogram is set,
  and it records an observation even when handling raises), and the
  multi-http-worker event loop (the shape used with
  `--detokenizer-worker-num > 1`) wraps its dispatch and fan-out in it,
  so both detokenizer loops report the metric.
- `docs/docs/references/production_metrics.mdx`: documents the new
  histogram, its semantics, and a p99 promql example.
- `test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py`: CPU unit
  tests driving both event loops with fake sockets: one observation per
  message, an observation is recorded when the handler raises, the
  disabled path still dispatches without observing, and the
  multi-worker loop records processing time.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: this change only adds observability. It does not touch
tokenization, detokenization, or model output logic; with metrics disabled
the event loops run the same code as before.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No server benchmark run. With `--enable-metrics` off, the added cost per
message is one attribute check in a context manager. With metrics on, it
is two `perf_counter` reads and one histogram observation per message,
the same pattern #45036 applies to the router loop. The detokenizer is
not the throughput-critical path this issue is about; the saturated stage
in the reported case was the router, whose identical instrumentation was
accepted as cheap enough there.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unit tests run locally on CPU:

```text
$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_multi_tokenizer_mixin.py
28 passed

$ python -m pytest test/registered/unit/managers/test_trim_matched_stop.py \
    test/registered/unit/managers/test_incremental_detokenize.py \
    test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_config_updates.py \
    test/registered/unit/managers/scheduler_components/test_output_sender.py
28 passed
```

@@ -7,6 +7,14 @@ SGLang exposes the following metrics via Prometheus. You can enable it by adding
 
 An example of the monitoring dashboard is available in [examples/monitoring/grafana.json](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/examples/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/json/sglang-dashboard.json).
 
+## Detokenizer processing time
+
+With `--enable-metrics`, each detokenizer worker exposes `sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds`, a histogram of the wall-clock time spent handling one received message: detokenizing the batch and sending the result onward, including blocking sends. It excludes waiting for and deserializing the incoming message, and it does not measure inter-process queue latency. Each message produces one observation, including messages whose handling raises an exception. A batch still produces one observation, so this is a per-message histogram, not a per-request latency metric. When metrics are disabled, the detokenizer creates no histogram and does not read the clock.
+
+```promql
+histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds_bucket[5m])))
+```
+
 ## Language model metrics
 
 `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` measures the time from request creation in the API server to the first token. For streaming requests it ends when the first output arrives after detokenization, which may contain no printable text. Non-streaming clients only see the final response, so for them it ends when the scheduler produced the first token.

 class MultiHttpWorkerDetokenizerMixin:
     """Mixin class for DetokenizerManager"""
 
+    @contextmanager
+    def _timed_processing(self: DetokenizerManager):
+        """Time one message's dispatch and send for the processing histogram.
+
+        The histogram is created by DetokenizerManager when metrics are
+        enabled. The receive wait happens before this context is entered, so
+        it is excluded. When metrics are disabled this is a no-op and the
+        clock is never read. A message whose handling raises still records
+        an observation.

+        histogram = getattr(self, "processing_seconds", None)
+        if histogram is None:
+            yield
+        else:
+            start = perf_counter()
+            try:
+                yield
+            finally:
+                histogram.observe(perf_counter() - start)

@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
+import contextlib
 import pickle
 import unittest
 from array import array
@@ -632,5 +633,133 @@ def test_event_loop_sends_one_message_per_owner(self):
         self.assertEqual(sent, [("worker-a", ["rid-0", "rid-1"])])
 
 
+class _FakeWatchdog:
+    def disable(self):
+        return contextlib.nullcontext()
+
+    def feed(self):
+        pass
+
+
+def _make_processing_histogram(registry):
+    from prometheus_client import Histogram
+
+    return Histogram(
+        "sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds",
+        "Time spent handling one received message in the detokenizer.",
+        buckets=(0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0),
+        registry=registry,
+    )
+
+
+def _make_detokenizer_manager(processing_seconds):
+    from sglang.srt.managers.detokenizer_manager import DetokenizerManager
+
+    manager = object.__new__(DetokenizerManager)
+    manager.soft_watchdog = _FakeWatchdog()
+    manager.processing_seconds = processing_seconds
+    manager.recv_from_scheduler = object()
+    manager.send_to_tokenizer = object()
+    manager._request_dispatcher = MagicMock(
+        return_value=SimpleNamespace(http_worker_ipcs=["ipc-a"])
+    )
+    return manager
+
+
+class TestDetokenizerProcessingMetrics(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_event_loop_records_one_observation_per_message(self):
+        from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry
+
+        from sglang.srt.managers import detokenizer_manager
+
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        manager = _make_detokenizer_manager(_make_processing_histogram(registry))
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                detokenizer_manager,
+                "sock_recv",
+                side_effect=[object(), object(), EOFError("end of input")],
+            ),
+            patch.object(detokenizer_manager, "sock_send") as send,
+            self.assertRaisesRegex(EOFError, "end of input"),
+        ):
+            manager.event_loop()
+
+        self.assertEqual(manager._request_dispatcher.call_count, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(send.call_count, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            registry.get_sample_value("sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds_count"),
+            2.0,
+        )
+
+    def test_event_loop_records_observation_when_handling_raises(self):
+        from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry
+
+        from sglang.srt.managers import detokenizer_manager
+
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        manager = _make_detokenizer_manager(_make_processing_histogram(registry))
+        manager._request_dispatcher = MagicMock(
+            side_effect=RuntimeError("handler failed")
+        )
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                detokenizer_manager, "sock_recv", side_effect=[object()]
+            ),
+            self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "handler failed"),
+        ):
+            manager.event_loop()
+
+        self.assertEqual(
+            registry.get_sample_value("sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds_count"),
+            1.0,
+        )
+
+    def test_event_loop_without_metrics_still_dispatches(self):
+        from sglang.srt.managers import detokenizer_manager
+
+        manager = _make_detokenizer_manager(None)
+        manager._request_dispatcher = MagicMock(return_value=None)
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                detokenizer_manager,
+                "sock_recv",
+                side_effect=[object(), EOFError("end of input")],
+            ),
+            patch.object(detokenizer_manager, "sock_send") as send,
+            self.assertRaisesRegex(EOFError, "end of input"),
+        ):
+            manager.event_loop()
+
+        self.assertEqual(manager._request_dispatcher.call_count, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(send.call_count, 0)
+
+    def test_multi_worker_loop_records_processing_time(self):
+        from prometheus_client import CollectorRegistry
+
+        from sglang.srt.managers import multi_tokenizer_mixin
+
+        registry = CollectorRegistry()
+        manager = _make_detokenizer_manager(_make_processing_histogram(registry))
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                multi_tokenizer_mixin,
+                "sock_recv",
+                side_effect=[_make_batch_str_output(), EOFError("end of input")],
+            ),
+            patch.object(
+                multi_tokenizer_mixin, "_send_output_to_tokenizer_workers"
+            ) as fan_out,
+            self.assertRaisesRegex(EOFError, "end of input"),
+        ):
+            manager.multi_http_worker_event_loop()
+
+        self.assertEqual(fan_out.call_count, 1)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            registry.get_sample_value("sglang:detokenizer_processing_seconds_count"),
+            1.0,
+        )
+
+
